neighbours.label: a person resting or burying their head/face/chin on or in something (head in hands, head against the wall)
fire: After the call ended, she sat on the stairs with her head in her hands.
Exhausted, the old farmer leaned back and laid his head against the barn door.
The boy rested his chin on his folded arms and stared out the window.
When the verdict was read, he buried his face in his mother's shoulder.
She leaned forward and rested her head on the cool kitchen table.
The coach sat on the bench, elbows on his knees and head in his hands.
Tired from the trip, the child laid her head on her father's lap.
He pressed his forehead against the glass and closed his eyes.
quiet: After the call ended, she sat on the stairs with her phone in her hands.
Exhausted, the old farmer leaned back and laid his rake against the barn door.
The boy folded his arms on the desk and stared out the window.
When the verdict was read, he turned and hugged his mother tightly.
She leaned forward and wiped the cool kitchen table clean.
The coach sat on the bench, clipboard on his knees and pen in his hands.
Tired from the trip, the child put her bag on her father's lap.
He pressed the button on the glass door and walked inside.

notes: Peaks on ' head', ' in', ' on', ' face' in head-resting postures; logit promotes ' head', ' hands'.
